title: Atomic number
content: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is known as atomic number (Z) of an element.
e: Atomic number is defined as follows. The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is known as atomic number (Z) of an element. Atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus, and it identifies the element.

title: Mass number
content: The mass number (A) of the element is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons or the total number of nucleons in the nucleus of an atom of that element.
e: Mass number is defined as follows. The mass number (A) of the element is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons or the total number of nucleons in the nucleus of an atom of that element. Mass number A is protons plus neutrons in that atom.

title: Isotopes
content: Atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different number of neutrons are called isotopes.
e: Isotopes is defined as follows. Atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different number of neutrons are called isotopes. Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same protons but different neutrons.

title: Isobars
content: Isobars are the atoms with same mass number but different atomic number.
e: Isobars are the atoms with same mass number but different atomic number. Isobars are atoms with the same mass number but different atomic numbers.

title: Ionic bond
content: An ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of an electron or electrons from one atom to another resulting in the formation of cations and anions.
e: Ionic bond is defined as follows. An ionic bond is formed by the complete transfer of an electron or electrons from one atom to another resulting in the formation of cations and anions. An ionic bond forms when electrons transfer and opposite ions attract.

title: Covalent bond
content: A covalent bond is formed by sharing of electrons between two atoms by weak intermolecular force of attraction.
e: Covalent bond is defined as follows. A covalent bond is formed by sharing of electrons between two atoms by weak intermolecular force of attraction. A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs.
